My typical daily carry is an M&P 9 Compact. In street clothes it goes IWB. In dress clothes, it's OWB with my sports coat covering it. It's small enough to easily conceal, but still has a decent ammo count. Plus, at the range, I can throw in full sized mags and have more fun.

I also have an M9 that I carry in a shoulder holster when I'm on long drives (travel for work). The M9 is the gun I am most accurate with, plus it's 17 rounds. I only really need it concealed when I stop at a gas station to use the bathroom.

So, what does voat carry and why?

I live in a state where 'carry' is limited to walking around on my own property, so my situation is pretty different than most.

That said, my preferred pistol is a Sig P250, a .40 compact slide over a subcompact grip. It's a simple, true-double-action pistol, no decockers, no external safety, no decisions about what mode to carry it in; it's basically a windex bottle that shoots hollow points.

I think of it as a modern rendition of the bulldog revolver, a short, chunky, powerful gun that's simplicity itself to use. It is heavy and thick and the trigger is not for everyone, but if you grew up on DA revolvers it will seem like second nature.
"Basicly a windex bottle that shoots hollow points." That is my favorite trigger pull description ever :)

My EDC is a Glock 36. It's only 6 +1 but it is .45 ACP. I use a Saf-T-Blok which assures no Plaxico leg for this old fart.

Galco USA 430 IWB is very comfortable.

Interesting, do you simply push the block out with your trigger finger? Ever have any problems of the block falling out unintentionally?

Also if you haven't seen this enjoy. Plaxico Burress' PSA on Gun Safety

The Saf-T-Blok has an adjustment screw to adjust tension. You adjust it to where it pops out with the appropriate sideways trigger finger pressure, I have not had an occasion where it fell out without me causing it to do so.

There has been a numerous "Glock Leg" incidents. It happens typically when holstering the piece and a belt, shirt tail, finger, etc. depresses the Glock trigger safety and then the trigger. Several other pistol manufacturers use the Glock trigger safety design in lieu of external safeties and they have the same opportunity to AD.

So I conceal carry at the 4 o'clock position. More of a chance of me getting "Glock Butt". I know some LEO's out there that crotch carry their backup piece. The Saf-T-Blok would seem an imperative in that case. Just saying...

The lack of an external safety is what has prevented me from getting a Glock. I like the 26 and the 43 the most. I have always been a 1911/USP guy but the price, simplicity, and availability of accessories for Glocks compels me to get one.

I became a 1911 fan back in the early 70's. I've owned a Model 70 and a Model 80 Colt, an AMT Longslide and a Kimber Super Carry Ultra. All traded off.

As far as Glocks are concerned, I've had a total of eight. Reliability is near 100%. I traded a Glock 30 for my 36 as it fits my hand better and conceals better. My wife has a 42.

You should try one. I think you would like it.

Since I have the 938 I probably won't be buying any pistols for a little while since it's just not in the budget. However my local FFL is having a BBQ dinner this weekend and raffling off a CORE 15 Hardcore X1 so maybe, if luck holds out, I'll have something new to post in /v/guns on Monday...
As an ex 1911 guy I'd strongly suggest looking at the Smith & Wesson M&P series, they are available with a 1911 style thumb safety and have a grip angle much closer to a 1911 than that on a glock.

My EDC is a Sig P938 SAS Imgur I & Imgur II. I have been in love lust with this gun ever since I held one at my local gun store. I keep it in a DeSantis Superfly holster in my pocket. It absolutely disappears in my pocket and if it ever imprints the extra fly on the DeSantis makes it look like a wallet in your pocket instead of a concealed pistol. Aside from it's ease of concealment the pistol is fantastic. I have put around 500 rds through it since I've owned it with no FTF/FTEs. I was also impressed by the lack of recoil and the accuracy from a 2-3/4" barrel. I use the 7+1 Sig mags with the pinky extension, makes all the difference even though after 500+ rounds I would feel comfortable shooting it with the regular mag due to the incredibly manageable recoil. Another benefit is availability/price of ammo over the .380 and the .40 S&W (My last pistol). They are particularly expensive at $838 MSRP but they usually run somewhere from $700-750 +Tax. I found mine on gunbroker from a high-volume dealer in PA and only paid $625 out the door including the $25 transfer fee from my local FFL.

TL:DR - EDC is a Sig P938 SAS and the rest of that mess up there is me expressing my love for it.
I have a Glock 42 and a spare magazine. It small and easy to EDC at work. I haven't found a holster that I like yet for my Sig 229, but I am looking because I like that pistol a bit more.
I run the same rig (M&P9) IWB 90% of the time, absolutely great gun.

Ruger SR9c, it's just the right size for me, it shoots smooth and easy, fits my hand, points naturally. I think that's mostly because it's grip angle is close to a 1911 which is what I'm used to. I can carry a spare SR9 magazine with 17rds and pop one in at home to turn it into my nightstand gun. Plus it was pretty darn cheap :)

P226 West German because it's been my constant companion for 10 years. I used to mix in a Charter Arms Bulldog, but my ex wife took it. Im looking at finding a lighter summergun and I might hold out for the back again P225.

What: A G19 with TLR-1HL, with either a Raven Concealment VG2 or Phantom LB.

Why: Because it's just small enough to conceal while wearing a t-shirt and just big enough to make me feel like I've brought enough gun. 15rds, weapons light, can get my whole hand around the grip. I am very accurate and quick with the G19. It would make me very nervous to take a shot in public with a pistol any smaller. My 2c.

Kahr CM9 with slide cerakoted black and with Dawson Precision night sights installed. I've stippled the grip and added a forward thumb rest. Usually carry with the factory flush mags but sometimes with the 7round extended mags or flush mag with pinky extension.

I've put probably 6-700 rounds through it now and still have had no failures. It functions as it should.

Shepherd Holster as well.
Glock 27 subcompact (9+1). 40cal is a good balance of stopping power/recoil/weight/size, and the short grip makes it quite compact and easy to carry.

Walther PPS in 9mm. I run the 7 round magazine and carry in a Remora tuckable or AG Cloak Tuck 2.0. I'm a fit, muscular guy so it has to be single stack to be concealable and the PPS fit my hand extremely well, had great sights right out of the box, and has a very nice trigger. I like the paddle mag release as well; my VP9 has the same so I'm really used to it and think it's better than the button release.
